sourceBasis: Full newsletter email; linked articles and episodes not independently reviewed.
mergePolicy: Union existing cards with new sources by title and canonical destination; never replace from Inbox alone.
zeroCardReview: One catch-up promotion reviewed; its main episode already appears in the October 30 edition. No new standalone editorial source or account-action notice.

cards.title: The US in Brief: After the tsunami
cards.preview: The newsletter reports a tech-stock sell-off as investors worry that new Democratic officeholders could curb data-centre expansion. It also follows pressure on administration officials and the Republican struggle over the party’s next presidential campaign.
cards.durationBasis: No article reading time supplied in the source email; no estimate inferred from teaser length

cards.title: Donald Trump’s humiliation offers America an opportunity
cards.preview: The weekly editor’s note argues that the midterm rebuke creates an opening to tackle corruption and everyday economic pressures. It weighs Democrats’ need to combine scrutiny with governing against Republican divisions and Trump’s continuing foreign-policy powers.
cards.durationBasis: No article reading time supplied in the source email; no estimate inferred from teaser length

cards.title: The US in Brief: Republicans crumble
cards.preview: The roundup follows Republican recriminations after the midterms, including J.D. Vance’s criticism of the Iran war. It also examines Democrats’ plans for congressional oversight and their expanded control of state governments.
cards.durationBasis: No article reading time supplied in the source email; no estimate inferred from teaser length

cards.title: The Insider: Is this the end of the Trump era?
cards.preview: John Prideaux introduces a panel with the US politics team on the midterm result and its consequences. The agenda covers Republican and Democratic divisions, the remaining Trump presidency and the contest for 2028.
cards.durationBasis: 45 minutes explicitly stated for this episode

cards.title: The US in Brief: A blue tsunami
cards.preview: The newsletter reports Democrats regaining both chambers of Congress and winning governorships in Republican strongholds. Its initial account highlights Texas and shifts among Hispanic and black voters, while noting that the party still lacks a veto-proof majority.
cards.durationBasis: No article reading time supplied in the source email; no estimate inferred from teaser length

cards.title: The US in Brief: What to look out for tonight
cards.preview: An election-day guide identifies the Senate battlegrounds and explains why the newsletter’s forecast is more cautious about Democrats than prediction markets. It also covers state ballot measures, challenges to vote counting and misleading AI campaign ads.
cards.durationBasis: No article reading time supplied in the source email; no estimate inferred from teaser length

cards.title: Inside Economics: Has Trumponomics delivered?
cards.preview: Henry Curr sets out questions for former White House economic adviser Pierre Yared about Trump’s economic record. The discussion asks whether the AI boom masks damage from tariffs, war and borrowing, and why strong growth has not reassured voters.
cards.durationBasis: 43 minutes stated for the matching on-demand Economics episode in the November 4 Insider email

cards.title: The US in Brief: A November surprise
cards.preview: The newsletter leads with Haley Stevens endorsing Republican Mike Rogers after losing Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary. It also tracks the Alaska ballot dispute and the state-government contests that could reshape election rules.
cards.durationBasis: No article reading time supplied in the source email; no estimate inferred from teaser length

cards.title: The quality you should most wish for your children
cards.preview: The Saturday newsletter explores an internal locus of control: the belief that personal choices can influence outcomes. It introduces Bartleby’s case for cultivating agency in children, alongside related columns on optimism and work.
